verses.1:1: The pronouncement of the word of the LORD to Israel by the hand of Malachi.
verses.1:2: "I have loved you," says the LORD. "Yet you say, 'In what way have You loved us?' Was Esau not a brother to Jacob?" declares the LORD. "Yet I loved Jacob,
verses.1:3: and Esau I hated; and I made his mountains a desolation and gave his inheritance to the jackals of the wilderness."
verses.1:4: Though Edom says, "We have been demolished, yet we will return and build up the ruins," this is what the LORD of hosts says: "They may build, but I will tear down; and people will call them 'Territory of Wickedness,' and 'The People against whom the LORD is indignant forever.'
verses.1:5: And your own eyes will see it, and you yourselves will say, 'The LORD is great beyond the territory of Israel!'"
verses.1:6: "A son honors a father, and a servant his master. If then I am a father, where is My honor? And if I am a master, where is the reverence due Me?" says the LORD of hosts to you, the priests who despise My name. "Yet you say, 'In what way have we despised Your name?'
verses.1:7: You are presenting defiled food on My altar! Yet you say, 'In what way have we defiled You?' By saying, 'The table of the LORD is despised.'
verses.1:8: And when you present a blind animal to sacrifice, is there no evil in that? And when you present a lame or sick one, is there no evil in that? Offer it now to your governor! Would he be pleased with you, or would he grant you favor?" says the LORD of hosts.
verses.1:9: And now, plead for the favor of God, that He may be gracious to us! "With this coming from your own hand, will He grant favor to any of you?" says the LORD of hosts.
verses.1:10: "Who is there even among you who would shut the doors, so that you would not kindle fire on My altar for nothing? I have no delight in you," says the LORD of hosts, "and I will not accept an offering from your hand.
verses.1:11: For from the sun's rising to its setting, My name is great among the nations, and in every place incense is presented to My name, along with a pure offering; for My name is great among the nations," says the LORD of hosts.
verses.1:12: "But you are profaning it when you say, 'The table of the Lord is defiled, and its produce, its food, is despised.'
verses.1:13: You also say, 'Look, what a weariness!' and you sniff at it," says the LORD of hosts. "And you bring what was seized by force, and the lame, and the sick; and thus you bring the offering! Should I accept it from your hand?" says the LORD.
verses.1:14: "And cursed is the deceiver who has a male in his flock and vows it, yet sacrifices what is blemished to the Lord! For I am a great King," says the LORD of hosts, "and My name is feared among the nations."
verses.2:1: "And now, this command is for you, priests.
verses.2:2: If you will not listen, and if you will not take it to heart to give honor to My name," says the LORD of hosts, "then I will send the curse among you and I will curse your blessings; indeed, I have already cursed them, because you are not taking it to heart.
verses.2:3: Look, I am about to rebuke your seed, and I will spread dung on your faces, the dung of your festivals; and you will be carried off with it.
verses.2:4: Then you will know that I have sent this command to you, so that My covenant with Levi may remain," says the LORD of hosts.
verses.2:5: "My covenant with him was one of life and peace, and I gave them to him for reverence; so he feared Me and before My name he was filled with awe.
verses.2:6: Instruction of truth was in his mouth, and wrongdoing was not found on his lips; in peace and uprightness he walked with Me, and many he turned back from iniquity.
verses.2:7: For a priest's lips should keep knowledge, and people should seek instruction from his mouth; for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts.
verses.2:8: But you yourselves have turned aside from the way; you have caused many to stumble in the instruction; you have corrupted the covenant of Levi," says the LORD of hosts.
verses.2:9: "So I also have made you despised and brought low before all the people, just as you are not keeping My ways, but are showing partiality in the instruction."
verses.2:10: Is there not one Father for all of us? Did not one God create us? Why do we break faith, each man with his brother, so as to profane the covenant of our fathers?
verses.2:11: Judah has broken faith, and an abomination has been done in Israel and in Jerusalem; for Judah has profaned what is holy to the LORD, which He loves, and has married the daughter of a foreign god.
verses.2:12: As for the man who does this, may the LORD cut off from the tents of Jacob both the one who wakes and the one who answers, and the one who presents an offering to the LORD of hosts.
verses.2:13: And this second thing you do: you cover the altar of the LORD with tears, with weeping and groaning, because He no longer turns toward the offering nor receives it favorably from your hand.
verses.2:14: Yet you say, "For what cause?" Because the LORD has borne witness between you and the wife of your youth, with whom you yourself have broken faith, even though she is your partner and the wife of your covenant.
verses.2:15: Did He not make them one, though a remnant of spirit belonged to Him? And why the one? He was seeking godly seed. Therefore guard yourselves in your spirit, and let none of you break faith with the wife of his youth.
verses.2:16: For He hates divorce, says the LORD, the God of Israel, and violence covers his garment, says the LORD of hosts. Therefore guard yourselves in your spirit, and do not break faith.
verses.2:17: You have wearied the LORD with your words. Yet you say, "In what way have we wearied Him?" In that you say, "Everyone who does evil is good in the eyes of the LORD, and in them He delights," or, "Where is the God of justice?"
verses.3:1: "Look, I am sending My messenger, and he will clear a way before Me. And suddenly the Lord whom you are seeking will come to His temple; and the messenger of the covenant in whom you delight—look, He is coming," says the LORD of hosts.
verses.3:2: But who can endure the day of His coming, and who can stand at His appearing? For He is like the fire of a refiner and like launderers' soap.
verses.3:3: And He will sit refining and purifying silver, and He will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and like silver, and they will be for the LORD ones who present an offering in righteousness.
verses.3:4: Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasant to the LORD, as in ancient days and as in earlier years.
verses.3:5: "Then I will draw near to you for judgment, and I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers, and against the adulterers, and against those who swear falsely, and against those who oppress the hired laborer in his wages, the widow, and the orphan, and those who turn aside the resident alien, and do not fear Me," says the LORD of hosts.
verses.3:6: "For I, the LORD, have not changed; and you, sons of Jacob, have not come to an end.
verses.3:7: Ever since the days of your fathers you have turned aside from My statutes and have not kept them. Turn back to Me, and I will turn back to you," says the LORD of hosts. "Yet you say, 'In what way shall we turn back?'
verses.3:8: Will a human being rob God? Yet you are robbing Me! Still you say, 'In what way have we robbed You?' In the tithe and the contribution!
verses.3:9: With a curse you are cursed, for you are robbing Me—the entire nation!
verses.3:10: Bring the entire tithe into the storehouse, so that there may be food in My house, and please test Me in this," says the LORD of hosts, "see if I will not open for you the windows of the heavens and pour out for you a blessing until there is no more room.
verses.3:11: And I will rebuke the devourer for your sake, so that it will not destroy for you the fruit of the soil, nor will the vine in the field drop its fruit for you," says the LORD of hosts.
verses.3:12: "Then all the nations will call you blessed, for you yourselves will be a land of delight," says the LORD of hosts.
verses.3:13: "Your words have been harsh against Me," says the LORD. "Yet you say, 'What have we spoken together against You?'
verses.3:14: You have said, 'It is futile to serve God; and what gain is it that we have kept His charge, and that we have walked mournfully before the LORD of hosts?
verses.3:15: And now we ourselves call the arrogant blessed; not only are those who practice wickedness built up, they even test God and escape!'"
verses.3:16: Then those who feared the LORD spoke together, each to his companion, and the LORD paid attention and heard it; and a scroll of remembrance was written before Him for those who fear the LORD and who value His name.
verses.3:17: "And they will be Mine," says the LORD of hosts, "on the day when I act, as a treasured possession; and I will have compassion on them, just as a man has compassion on his son who serves him.
verses.3:18: Then you will see once more the difference between the righteous and the wicked, between the one who serves God and the one who has not served Him.
verses.3:19: For look, the day is coming, burning like an oven, when all the arrogant and everyone who practices wickedness will become stubble; and the coming day will set them on fire," says the LORD of hosts, "so that it will leave them neither root nor branch.
verses.3:20: Yet for you who fear My name, the sun of righteousness will shine forth with healing in its wings; and you will go out and leap like calves from the stall.
verses.3:21: And you will trample the wicked, for they will be ashes beneath the soles of your feet on the day when I act," says the LORD of hosts.
verses.3:22: "Look, I am sending Elijah the prophet to you before the coming of the day of the LORD, great and awesome.
verses.3:23: And he will turn back the heart of fathers to children, and the heart of children to their fathers, so that I will not come and strike the land with utter destruction.
verses.3:24: Remember the law of Moses My servant, which I commanded him at Horeb for all Israel—statutes and judgments."

notes.1:1: Hebrew massa literally means 'burden,' used as a technical term for a prophetic pronouncement. The prophet's name Malachi literally means 'My messenger,' anticipating the same Hebrew form in 3:1.
notes.1:3: Hebrew tannot is a rare feminine plural of tan ('jackals'), occurring only here in the Masoretic Text.
notes.1:8: The idiom 'grant favor' renders Hebrew nasa panim, literally 'lift up the face,' which recurs in 1:9 and carries the negative sense of 'showing partiality' in 2:9.
notes.1:11: The verbless clause 'My name is great' and the Hophal participles 'incense is presented' (muqtar muggash) are rendered in the present tense to match the nominal Hebrew syntax, though they can also carry futuristic force.
notes.1:13: Masoretic Hebrew reads 'sniff at it' (oto), referring to the Lord's table or service; rabbinic scribal tradition (tiqqun sopherim) notes an older reading 'at Me.'
notes.2:3: Masoretic Hebrew reads 'rebuking for you the seed' (et-hazzera), which can denote either priestly descendants or sown grain. The final verb is an impersonal third-person singular Qal (wenasa, literally 'and one will carry you away to/with it').
notes.2:12: Hebrew er weoneh, literally 'one who wakes and one who answers,' is an idiomatic merism meaning every living person or descendant without exception.
notes.2:15: The Hebrew of the first half is highly compressed and syntactically difficult; an alternative reading takes 'the One' as the subject throughout ('Did not the One make them, and a remnant of spirit belongs to Him? And what does the One seek?'). At the end of the verse, Hebrew shifts from second-person singular ('your youth') to a third-person singular jussive ('let him not break faith').
notes.2:16: Masoretic Hebrew has the third-person singular Qal perfect sane ('He hates') with the Piel infinitive construct shallach ('sending away/divorce'), followed by Piel perfect wekhissah ('and violence covers his garment' or 'and he covers his garment with violence'). The subject of sane is not expressed; the clause can also be read with the husband as subject ('the one who hates and divorces covers his garment with violence').
notes.3:1: Hebrew ha-adon ("the Lord" / "the sovereign") carries the definite article and is paired with "the messenger of the covenant" (mal'akh habberit); whether the final clause ("look, He is coming") identifies the messenger of the covenant with the Lord or refers to a distinct figure is debated, so the capitalization of pronouns reflects an interpretive editorial choice.
notes.3:8: The rare Hebrew verb qaba ('rob, defraud') occurs in the Hebrew Bible only here, in 3:9, and in Proverbs 22:23.
notes.3:10: The phrase 'until there is no more room' renders Hebrew ad-beli-day, literally 'until without sufficiency,' an idiom for overflowing abundance beyond capacity.
notes.3:13: The Niphal stem of dabar ('speak') here and in 3:16 carries reciprocal force, denoting people conversing together among themselves.
notes.3:17: Hebrew segullah ('treasured possession') can modify 'they will be Mine' with oseh ('when I act') used absolutely as in 3:21, or serve as the direct object of oseh ('on the day when I prepare a treasured possession').
notes.3:23: Native Masoretic order closes the book with this verse (3:24); in the Saints.Bible parallel display, MT 3:24 maps to slot 3:23 and MT 3:22 maps to slot 3:24. "Utter destruction" renders Hebrew cherem, the covenant ban of total destruction.
notes.3:24: Native Masoretic order places this command at 3:22 before the Elijah oracle (3:23–24). In the Saints.Bible parallel display, MT 3:22 maps to slot 3:24 and MT 3:23–24 map to slots 3:22–23.
